about.title: Fortuna Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: A job injury in Fortuna often gets funneled straight into the workers' compensation system, and for most employees that's the only path available against their employer, regardless of who was at fault. But that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, delivery driver, or property owner outside your own company contributed to what happened, a separate claim against that third party may be possible alongside your comp benefits. This matters in a town like Fortuna, where small crews, agricultural operations, retail storefronts along Main Street, and light industrial work near 12th Street often mean multiple companies and contractors are present on the same job site. Sorting out who's responsible for what isn't something you should have to figure out alone. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise results — we simply connect injured workers with an independent attorney who can review the details and explain what avenues, if any, apply to your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney First

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California generally treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — like a contractor or equipment maker — can still be pursued separately. An attorney can help identify whether that applies to your case.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: You typically have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and missing that window can complicate your claim. Getting guidance early helps protect your options.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing workers for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can explain your protections.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Rohnerville Road involving a subcontractor's equipment. Do I only have workers' comp?
items.answer: Not necessarily. If a subcontractor or another company's equipment contributed to your injury, you may have a separate third-party claim in addition to workers' comp. An independent attorney can look at the site setup and contracts involved to determine if that applies.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer in Fortuna?
items.answer: California generally requires injured workers to notify their employer within 30 days of the injury. Waiting longer can create complications, so it's best to report as soon as you're able and document what happened.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: No, retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an attorney can help you understand your options and protections.
